Bayesian probability spectrum

Source: R/bayes_spectrum.R
bayes_spectrum.Rd

Calculates the Bayesian probability spectrum of Gregory (2005) as used by Weedon et al. (2019) and Weedon (2020): the data are pre-whitened with the lag-1 autocorrelation coefficient, linearly detrended, tapered with a 5% split cosine taper and standardised; the variance-normalised Lomb-Scargle periodogram (routine PERIOD of Press et al., 1992) is then converted into the posterior probability of a single sinusoid at each frequency, \(p(f) \propto (1 - 2 P(f) / (N \overline{d^2}))^{(2 - N)/2}\), normalised so that the probabilities sum to one. Translated from Acycle v3.1 specbayes.m (Mingsong Li, after the FORTRAN program of Graham P. Weedon).

Usage

bayes_spectrum(data = NULL, genplot = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)

Arguments

data

Record to analyse (matrix or data frame with two columns: depth or time in column 1, proxy value in column 2; further columns are ignored). Rows are sorted on the first column and rows with non-finite values are removed; uneven spacing is allowed (Lomb-Scargle periodogram). Required, no default (Default=NULL gives an error).

genplot

Plot the periodogram and the Bayesian probability against frequency (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

verbose

Print the maximum probability and its frequency and period (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

Value

A list with elements freq (frequencies), period (1/freq), power (variance-normalised Lomb-Scargle periodogram of the pre-whitened, detrended, tapered and standardised data), bayes_prob (normalised Bayesian probability), max_prob, freq_max (frequency of maximum probability) and rho1 (lag-1 autocorrelation used for pre-whitening).

References

Gregory, P.C., 2005. Bayesian Logical Data Analysis for the Physical Sciences. Cambridge University Press.

Press, W.H., Teukolsky, S.A., Vetterling, W.T., Flannery, B.P., 1992. Numerical Recipes in FORTRAN, 2nd ed. Cambridge University Press.

Weedon, G.P., Page, K.N., Jenkyns, H.C., 2019. Cyclostratigraphy, stratigraphic gaps and the duration of the Hettangian (Jurassic): insights from the Blue Lias Formation of Southern Britain. Geological Magazine 156, 1469-1509.

Weedon, G.P., 2020. Confirmed detection of Palaeogene and Jurassic orbitally-forced sedimentary cycles in the depth domain using False Discovery Rates and Bayesian probability spectra. Boletin Geologico y Minero 131, 207-230.

Author

Michiel Arts (R translation); original MATLAB code: Mingsong Li, translated from the FORTRAN program of Graham P. Weedon.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(2)
n <- 400
t <- 1:n
noise <- as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(n), 0.5,
  method = "recursive"))
x <- noise + 1.5 * sin(2 * pi * t / 23)
res <- bayes_spectrum(data = cbind(t, x), genplot = TRUE)

1 / res$freq_max
#> [1] 23.47059
# }
